claim.claim-text: 1. A telescoping wing (110) system for an unmanned aerial vehicle, UAV, comprising:

a first wing (110) section comprising a substantially hollow interior; and a second wing (110) section configured to be stowed within the interior of the first wing (110) section such that an external surface of the second wing (110) section is adjacent to an internal surface of the first wing (110) section, wherein the second wing (110) section is attached to a fuselage (106) of an aerial vehicle and has a lesser chord length than the first wing (110) section, wherein the first wing (110) section and the second wing (110) section form a first wingspan in a first arrangement, the first arrangement comprising the second wing (110) section stowed within the interior of the first wing (110) section, and wherein the first wing (110) section and the second wing (110) section form a second wingspan in a second arrangement, the second arrangement comprising the first wing (110) section displaced along at least a portion of a length between a first end and a second end of the second wing (110) section, wherein the length of an exposed portion of the second wing (110) section increases as the first wing (110) section is displaced.

2. The telescoping wing (110) system of claim 1, wherein at least a portion of the first wingspan and the second wingspan of the aerial vehicle is comprised of approximately a length of the first wing (110) section and a length of an exposed portion of the second wing (110) section.

3. The telescoping wing (110) system of claim 1, wherein the length of the exposed portion of the second wing (110) section increases as the first wing (110) section is displaced by at least a portion of the length between the first end and the second end of the second wing (110) section in the second arrangement.

4. The telescoping wing (110) system of claim 3, wherein the displacement of the first wing (110) section along the length of the second wing (110) section extends the first wingspan of the aerial vehicle by approximately the displacement length to form the second wingspan.
5. The telescoping wing (110) system of claim 1, wherein the second wing (110) section comprises:

an actuator (210) configured at approximately the first end of the second wing (110) section and configured to drive a first pulley (325), and a second pulley (325) configured at approximately the second end of the second wing (110) section.

6. The telescoping wing (110) system of claim 5, further comprising: a belt (330) configured around the first pulley (325) and the second pulley (325), spanning at least a portion of the external surface between the first end and the second end of the second wing (110) section, wherein a segment of the belt (330) is attached to the first wing (110) section such that, upon actuation, a displacement of the attached segment of the belt (330) causes the first wing (110) section to traverse at least the portion of the length between the first end and the second end of the second wing (110) section.
7. The telescoping wing (110) system of claim 6, wherein the belt (330) further comprises notches to enable the actuator (210) to move the belt (330) upon actuation.

8. The telescoping wing (110) system of claim 7, wherein the belt (330) comprises a length of fibrous material, and wherein a first end of the fibrous material and a second end of the fibrous material are connected at the segment of the belt (330) that attaches to the interior surface of the first wing (110) section.
9. A telescoping wing (110) system for an unmanned aerial vehicle, UAV, comprising:
10. The telescoping wing (110) system of claim 9, wherein the interior of the outer section (310) is not obstructed by the control surface.

11. The telescoping wing (110) system of claim 10, wherein the control surface is configured to attach to the trailing-edge of the outer section (310), via the externally mounted hinge, so as to maximize the interior volume of the outer section (310).

12. The telescoping wing (110) system of claim 11, wherein the telescoping means is enabled to provide an improved wingspan ratio between the first configuration (102) and the second configuration (106) due to, at least in part, the inner section (305) being configurable within the interior of the outer section (310) without obstruction from the control surface attachment.

13. The telescoping wing (110) system of claim 12, wherein a surface area ratio between the inner section (305) and outer section (310) is increased due to, at least in part, the inner section (305) being configurable within the interior of the outer section (310) without obstruction from the control surface attachment.
14. The telescoping wing (110) system of claim 10, further comprising a servo (410) for actuating the control surface.
15. The telescoping wing (110) system of claim 10, wherein the control surface is configured to actuate regardless of a position of the outer section (310) relative to the inner section (305).
